items.text: ST0002 on vc's brief (hv's go of 2026-11-13, given live by vc): which, predict, the TUI's next marker and the Herdr mod. Order: WP01; WP02 and WP04; WP03, WP05 and WP06; WP08; WP07 last. Each WP in its own worktree under ~/Devel/scratch/ccusage-ic/ on branch ic/ST0002-NN, one Desk cargo slot (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=~/Devel/scratch/ccusage-ic/target) for its measured run, then the hand-over to vc. WHERE EACH STANDS: WP01 to WP04 done, closed by vc. WP05 (predict, with WP03's two text follow-ups) and WP06 (the next marker) are built and stacked, eade2e4, 95b7b3b and ef41e1b on main's fac240d, waiting for one Desk slot (01M7A1JYDSQNNHNNN55ACXCX40), first in line once hv's devvm build frees the cargo lane; cc signed predict's arithmetic. WP08 (the Herdr mod, the herdr verb and the TUI's refresh) is built on top, 7bd2655 and e2760d4; herdr-app check passes on a scratch copy; its verb's spelling is with vc for hv. WP07, the docs, comes last.
which --use (ST0002/WP03) calls the one use function cc makes in ST0003/WP03's first commit; ic writes no second. Released when that function is on main.

which --json's code (ST0002/WP03) waits for cc's sign-off of the shape ic sent. vc said yes with three changes: (a) rank null for unknown accounts; (b) resets_at as the endpoint gives it, to the second, the minute rounding kept inside the rule; (c) headroom under --model as cc defines it (vc suggested weekly terms). Released when cc has signed; then ic sends vc the final shape, which vc gives geodica-estate.

which --json version 1 is agreed: vc's yes with three changes (rank null for unknown; resets_at as the endpoint gives it, cut to the second; headroom as cc defines it) and cc's yes with three meanings (headroom in percent of the weekly allowance, under --model the lesser with the scoped window's share; scoped entries carry share; soonest among accounts not unknown). The final shape is in vc's inbox from ic, with one clarification open to objection: percent and resets_at report what the data says, and state and cause say whether the rule could use it.

ST0002/WP02 (ca09eae..fdfe1e5 on branch ic/ST0002-02) lands on main once cc signs the rule's meaning. Released when cc's yes is in ic's inbox; then ic lands it, mints AC-02.1 to AC-02.4's ATs, and tells vc.

ST0002/WP02 lands after hv's compact (vc's word), with three commits added to its range first, which ride on its run (vc): (a) vc's share leniency: a malformed weekly_scoped_shares, a bad entry or a share outside 0..100 leaves those windows with no share instead of refusing the snapshot, a unit test per malformed form, and under --model the reason says the model's share is unknown instead of a bare eligible; (b) cc's tightening: soonest is taken among usable accounts whose weekly window gives a reset, none when none does; (c) cc's text nit: an undated choice's reason says no eligible account gives a weekly reset. Then rebase on main, land, mint AC-02.1 to 02.4's ATs with id comments over their tests, intent at lint ST0002 clean, and tell vc what the new commits ran with. Released when the compact is done and vc's go to continue is in.

ST0002/WP04 design, decided before the fold: src/history.rs; a Sample is an account, a usage::Window and sampled_at; history.jsonl in the state dir, read with storage::read_optional, rewritten whole with storage::write_atomic, under a File::lock (flock) on history.lock, not auth_lock (Claude Code's protocol, and cc's); a mirror Line struct on disk (account, kind, model, percent, share, resets_at RFC 3339, sampled_at), unknown fields ignored for mixed brew and dev builds; Kind::name and Kind::from_name as the one name mapping, used by parse_windows too; usage::WEEK defined once; keep a window's first sample, then one per changed percent, the same window while Window::reset_minute is unchanged; drop samples older than WEEK, never at a reset; the hook in Client::load's Fetch::Success arm, a failed write joining the report's error beside the cache's ('usage fetched, but ...'); Client gains an endpoint field so a loopback unit test proves a fetch records and a cache hit does not; doctor's file_check covers history.jsonl; tests per the WP: unchanged percent, age drop vs reset kept, 0600, concurrent writers, only the windows' fields in each line.

ST0002/WP05's run carries two WP03 follow-ups from vc (inbox 2026-11-13, after its PASS of WP03 and WP04): (1) a line gives the headroom as what is below the cap, eg hello: 73% used, 22% below the 95% cap, resets in 3d04h, since hv reads left as what remains of the allowance; (2) hv's ruling 3, that ccusage works for any Claude account and shows whatever it reports: which's text lists an unknown account with the windows it does report, and a CLI test shows an account with a session window only listed as unknown with it, and never chosen.

ST0002/WP05 follow-up, once cc's tier recording lands (cc's todo 3, which vc sequences): predict sums the accounts of the most common subscriptionType and rateLimitTier pair among those the rule can use, compared whole; a tie goes to the active account's tier, else to the lexically first pair (cc's meaning); every other account is left out as another plan's allowance, and the text drops its one-plan assumption.

ic to cc and vc: the which --json shape for your read before WP03's code (ST0002/WP03: cc signs what it means, ic its shape, and geodica-estate reads it). Draft version 1, on the worked example's windows, with "..." where the record gives no value:

{"version": 1, "now": "2026-11-13T05:27:00Z", "cap": 95, "model": null,
 "active": "hello", "choice": "hello", "activated": false,
 "soonest": {"name": "hello", "resets_at": "2026-11-16T10:00:00Z"},
 "accounts": [
  {"name": "hello", "state": "chosen", "rank": 1, "percent": 73, "headroom": 22,
   "resets_at": "2026-11-16T10:00:00Z", "reason": "soonest reset with headroom", "cause": null,
   "scoped": [{"model": "Fable", "percent": ..., "resets_at": ...}], "session": null,
   "fetched_at": ..., "error": null},
  {"name": "engineering04", "state": "eligible", "rank": 2, "percent": 22, "headroom": 73, ...},
  ... ]}

What each field means:
- version: 1. A field added keeps it; a field removed, renamed or given a new meaning raises it. Readers ignore fields they do not know.
- now: when the rule ran. Every time is RFC 3339 UTC to the second with a Z, the form JavaScript's Date.parse is required to read, which the Herdr panel needs.
- cap: the cap in force, from config.toml or the one default.
- model: the --model given, spelled as the scoped windows spell it, else null.
- active: the active account after the call, else null.
- choice: the chosen account, else null.
- activated: true only when --use was given and this call made the choice active. False when --use was not given, when nothing is eligible, and when the choice was already active.
- soonest: the account whose weekly reset is soonest among those known, with that reset; null when none is known. The text names it when nothing is eligible.
- accounts: every account, in the text's order: chosen, eligible, at cap, unknown.
  - state: chosen, eligible, at_cap or unknown.
  - rank: the 1-based position in this list.
  - percent: weekly_all's percent used; null when there is no usable window.
  - headroom: the cap minus percent, never below 0. QUESTION FOR CC: under --model, is it the lesser of the weekly window's and that model's scoped window's? I propose yes: it is the room before the rule moves on, and WP02's tie-break on most headroom would use the same number.
  - resets_at: weekly_all's reset as the rule ranks it, rounded to the nearest minute; null when it has none.
  - reason: the one line the text prints for this account.
  - cause: for unknown only, one of error (no usable snapshot, and the report's error says why), stale (older than the cache's lifetime), reset_passed or no_weekly_window; null otherwise. A script never has to parse reason.
  - scoped: each weekly_scoped window as {model, percent, resets_at}, model null when the endpoint names none. Ranked on only under --model.
  - session: {percent, resets_at} when the endpoint returns a session window, else null. Never ranked.
  - fetched_at: when the account's data was fetched, else null.
  - error: the report's own error line, else null, eg "usage rate limited; retry in 28m", which the panel shows as it is.

Exit codes: 0 with a choice, 1 with none. The JSON goes to stdout either way, and the one-line reason to stderr.

Why each account's windows are in it: on its timer the Herdr panel then calls which --json and predict --json alone, and usage --all --json only when someone opens an account's detail.

Reply yes, or with the changes. cc: the rule's meaning (WP02's record) is for your sign-off at WP02's hand-over, unless you want to change it now.

ic to cc: ST0002/WP02's rule is ready for your sign-off on its meaning, which you asked to give at the hand-over. It is on branch ic/ST0002-02, ca09eae..fdfe1e5 (on main's 0da313c), green on its Desk run, and it lands once you sign.

Read src/which.rs; choose's doc comment is the rule in one paragraph. What it implements:
- Usable: the report holds a snapshot fetched within the cache's lifetime (usage::fresh with usage::TTL, passed as the argument), with a weekly_all window whose reset is still ahead. A fresh snapshot is usable even when the report carries an error, as when only the cache save failed.
- Unknown, never chosen, with a cause: error (no snapshot, or one that will not parse), stale (fetched a whole lifetime ago or more, or at a time ahead of now), no_weekly_window, reset_passed (the reset's exact instant is at or before now). Checked in that order.
- Eligible: usable, weekly percent below the cap, and with a model named, that model's scoped window below the cap too, matched by name regardless of case. An account with no scoped window for the model is bounded by the weekly window alone. At cap otherwise.
- Headroom, your meaning: the cap minus the weekly percent; under a model, the lesser of that and (the cap minus the scoped percent) x share / 100; floored at 0; 0 at the cap; none when unknown, and none under a model when the scoped window has no share.
- Rank: eligible first, by the weekly reset rounded to the nearest minute (Window::reset_minute, which history will use too), then most headroom with none after a known one, then name. At-cap accounts follow by reset, then name. A weekly window with no reset ranks after every dated one. Unknown accounts come last, by name, with no rank.
- The choice is the first eligible account. soonest is the ranked account (so not unknown) with the soonest reset as the rule orders resets, the higher ranked on a tie.

Reply yes, or with what to change. Noted from your message: which --use calls switch::to in ST0002/WP03, and ST0003/WP03's new use text comes to me to sign when you have it.

- WHAT IT IS: src/history.rs. record keeps a window's first sample, then one each time its percent changes, a window being the same window while its kind, and its reset to the minute (WP02's Window::reset_minute), are unchanged. Samples go by age alone, once older than usage::WEEK, which is defined once, and never at a reset. The file is history.jsonl in the state directory, 0600, read through storage::read_optional and rewritten whole through storage::write_atomic, under an flock on history.lock (std's File::try_lock, waited for five seconds at most, after which that fetch goes unrecorded and says so). A line holds account, kind, model, percent, share, resets_at and sampled_at, and nothing else from the response. A line of a kind this build does not know, as a later build may write, is kept as it is; a line it cannot read refuses the file, naming the line and never its text, with the remedy. Kind::name and Kind::from_name are the one mapping between kinds and their names, and parse_windows now uses it too. history::samples reads the history back, for predict.
- THE HOOK: Client::load's success arm keeps the fetch through one function, keep, which saves the cache and records the history. Either failure joins the report's error, eg "usage fetched, but could not record history: ...", and the usage stands. A cache hit or a cooldown never reaches it. doctor's private-file check covers history.jsonl, and the README's XDG table names it.
- ONE CHANGE FROM MY DESIGN: there is no endpoint field on Client, and no loopback test through load. A unit test through load would run /usr/bin/security against the real login keychain's search list, because on macOS auth::read looks for the profile's Keychain item before its file, and dc's watch-out keeps that out of tests. An endpoint override in the binary would also give the bearer token a new route. So keep is tested directly (AT-04.1), and a CLI test, whose binary runs under the sandbox's HOME as every CLI test does, shows a cache hit and a cooldown record nothing (AT-04.4).
- ACCEPTANCE: AT-04.1 (a fetch records, and a failed record keeps the usage), AT-04.2 (first sample, then one per change), AT-04.3 (a 0600 file in the state directory), AT-04.4 (a cache hit records nothing) and AT-04.5 (age, not reset) cover AC-04.1 and are green on this run, each with its id comment over its test. ic to cc: ST0002/WP05's arithmetic, predict, whose meaning you sign before it lands. I am building it on this reading now, so say early if any of it is wrong.
- RATE: percent of one weekly allowance a used per elapsed hour, as vc proposed and hv read: the rises in weekly_all across all accounts, divided by the hours the history spans. A rise is the climb between consecutive samples of one account's one window (a fall counts as none), and across a reset it is the next window's first percent, since that window began at 0 after the last sample of the one before. An account's first sample in the history adds nothing, since what came before it is unknown. The span runs from the first weekly_all sample to the last, across all accounts. The report gives the samples and hours it rests on.
- TOO LITTLE: a span under one day, defined once, or no rise at all, and predict says so, projects nothing and exits 0. One day, so a span takes in a day's working and idle hours at least once.
- SIMULATION: from now to the horizon, the last of the usable accounts' current resets, event by event. At each step which::choose itself, on the projected state, picks the account, which climbs at the rate until it reaches the cap or a reset comes. A window that resets starts again at 0, with its reset a week on. Each account's projected percent is taken at its current reset, and its unused percent is 100 less that, so it includes the share above the cap that the rule leaves. The total is the sum, in percent of one weekly allowance, since the accounts are on one plan.
- LEFT OUT: an account the rule cannot use now, with its reason. A free-plan account falls there, since its usage gives no weekly window or none at all. Nothing in the response names a plan, so that is the only test I have; say if you know a better one.
- JSON: versioned as which's is; its shape comes with the hand-over.
